name: qualify-async-fanout-py
note: Expected: good, good-asyncio, good-workers, and good-strict-api pass (good-strict-api changes the gateway module's signatures, so the fixture_tests measure fails while existing_commands_unchanged passes); sequential fails within_budget only (it finishes well before the hard limit, so its report is judged and right); unbounded, default-pool (a thread pool of Python's default size, 32 with the check's PYTHON_CPU_COUNT), and affinity-pool (one worker per CPU the command may use, more than 16 wherever the run is valid) fail within_limit and the two report checks (the gateway answers 429 past 16); no-timeout fails within_budget, failures_handled (offline docks printed as failed with HTTP 504 after the gateway's 60 s), and no_held_requests; abandoned fails within_limit, within_budget, no_held_requests, and the report checks; abandoned-daemon and abandoned-daemon-cap10 fail within_limit and the report checks (abandoned requests pile up past 16 in the outage whatever the sweep's own cap) but exit on time, and may also fail no_held_requests (a request they gave up on stays in progress until they exit); paced fails within_limit and the report checks (no bound on requests in progress); pool-holds fails no_held_requests (its 16 workers stay on silent docks' requests for 30 s in the outage; it never goes over the limit, and within_budget depends on whether the outage's time limit falls below its 35 s); overall-deadline fails answered_docks_correct, failures_handled, and no_held_requests; long-timeout fails failures_handled and no_held_requests (late docks printed as readings, offline docks' requests held 10 s); leaks fails no_work_after_exit only; wrong fails failures_handled only; noop fails everything but existing_commands_unchanged. Command arms need no toolchain: the check runs everything. The run is invalid on a host where the check sees 16 CPUs or fewer.
